pool.text: Mathilda began the first oil drilling in Balikpapan on 10 February.
The Dutch East Indies colonial administration granted township status to Balikpapan.
Bataafsche Petroleum Maatschappij made Balikpapan its headquarters and imported overseas laborers.
The oldest refinery in the area was founded in Balikpapan.
The Empire of Japan occupied Balikpapan during World War II.
A Japanese invasion convoy arrived at Balikpapan and faced United States destroyers.
The American 380th Bombardment Group attacked the oil refineries in Balikpapan.
The Battle of Balikpapan concluded the Borneo campaign and Allied forces took control.
Royal Dutch Shell completed major repairs to the oil production area in Balikpapan.
The CIA attacked Balikpapan and stopped oil exports from the city.
Pertamina took control over the ownership of BPM and its oil exploration activities.
Balikpapan II refinery opened and produced petrol, LPG, naphtha, kerosene, and diesel fuel.
The urban forest in Telagasari was inaugurated with an area of 29.4 hectares.
The Wain River forest and Manggar River forest were hit by a fire in Balikpapan.
Balikpapan toppled Yogyakarta as the best city for living based on the index.
Balikpapan was named the best city for living on the Indonesian Most Liveable City Index.
Balikpapan Botanical Garden located at kilometer 15 was officially opened.
Balikpapan was recognized as the Most Loveable City as part of the Earth Hour City Challenge.
Balikpapan was nominated for the second time as the most lovable and sustainable city.
Balikpapan City Trans served the city with 3 corridors since its auguration.
